label: Walter Haut
narrative: Walter G. Haut (3 June 1922 - 15 December 2005) wrote the sentence that started all of it. A bombardier who flew thirty-five missions against Japan and dropped instrument packages at the Bikini tests in 1946, he became public information officer for the 509th Bomb Group at Roswell Army Air Field, and on 8 July 1947 base commander Col. William H. Blanchard - a close personal friend - told him to write and distribute a release stating the field had come into possession of a flying disc. He did, and the story went round the world before Fort Worth retracted it the same day. Haut's own testimony evolved in a documented, dateable sequence that this board records in full because the sequence is the evidence. In 1980's 'The Roswell Incident' he is explicitly 'not a witness.' In 1979 and again in a March 1989 interview he said he knew nothing of what was recovered and had been refused when he asked to see it. In a sworn affidavit signed 14 May 1993 he added that Blanchard must have seen the material himself and that neither Blanchard nor Marcel could have mistaken it for a weather balloon. Then, in December 2002, Donald Schmitt composed and emailed a further affidavit which Haut signed at the International UFO Museum in front of his daughter Julie Shuster and a notary, on the agreement that it would not be released until after his death; it asserts first-hand sight of a craft and bodies. Haut died in 2005 and the document was published by Carey and Schmitt in 'Witness to Roswell' (2007). A witness whose claims escalate monotonically over twenty-two years, with the largest escalation drafted by his interviewer and embargoed until he could not be cross-examined, is a specific kind of evidence, and this board grades it as such.

timeline.label: RAAF press release
timeline.text: Walter Haut, public information officer of the 509th Bomb Group, writes and distributes the release announcing that Roswell Army Air Field has come into possession of a flying disc, naming Maj. Jesse Marcel Sr. as the recovering officer. Fort Worth retracts it the same day.

timeline.label: Haut's sworn affidavit
timeline.text: Walter Haut signs an affidavit stating that Col. Blanchard saw the material, that there is no chance Blanchard would have mistaken it for a weather balloon and none that Marcel would have been mistaken.

timeline.label: The sealed Haut affidavit
timeline.text: Donald Schmitt composes and emails a further affidavit which Haut signs at the International UFO Museum before his daughter and a notary, embargoed until after his death. It asserts first-hand sight of a craft and bodies, contradicting his 1979, 1989 and 1993 statements.

unverified: The claim that Col. Blanchard personally dictated the press release rests on Haut's posthumous affidavit alone
Whether the 2002 document was executed with the formalities of an affidavit under New Mexico law; the notarisation is attested but the jurat has not been examined here.
